language_wrapper: In a math contest, define F(r, c, k) as the number of black/white colorings of an r×c toroidal chessboard (rows and columns wrap around cyclically) such that: (i) no two black cells are horizontally or vertically adjacent (including wrap-around), and (ii) between any two consecutive rows, no two black cells are diagonally adjacent in either direction (both NE and NW are forbidden, with indices taken modulo r and c). Additionally, the first row contains exactly k black cells. Given c = {cols}, k = {k}, and r ranging from {rows_min} to {rows_max} inclusive, compute S = ∑_{r={rows_min}}^{rows_max} F(r, {cols}, {k}).
hardness_rationale: Compared to the seed problem (independent sets on an n×n grid with only orthogonal adjacency and non-wrapping boundaries), this family enforces toroidal wrap-around in both directions and forbids diagonal adjacencies between consecutive rows. The required count is further constrained by a fixed cardinality for the first row. Solving any instance demands a transfer-matrix approach with cyclic closure conditions (to enforce the torus), significantly increasing state management and requiring careful handling of circular shifts. Summing across multiple board heights compounds the complexity, making guessing infeasible.
notes: Proof of correctness: Model each row as a bitmask over c columns. A row is valid iff it has no horizontally adjacent 1s, including wrap-around, which is exactly enforced by (mask & ((mask << 1) & bitmask)) == 0 and the end-pair check between bits 0 and c−1. Between consecutive rows a and b, the constraints of no vertical and no diagonal adjacency in either direction are exactly captured by (a & b) == 0, (a & shift_left_c(b)) == 0, and (a & shift_right_c(b)) == 0 using circular shifts, reflecting toroidal columns. For a height r torus, the last row must also be compatible with the first row, so the same adjacency checks apply to the pair (last, first), closing the cycle. The number F(r, c, k) is obtained by summing over all valid first rows s with popcount(s) = k and counting length-(r−1) paths in the transfer graph starting at s, then imposing the closure condition at the end. Since every coloring of the torus corresponds bijectively to such a cyclic sequence of row masks with the stipulated constraints and first-row cardinality, the DP computes the exact count. Summing over r in the specified range yields S. This transfer-matrix formulation is standard for hard combinatorial tilings and independent-set counts on periodic lattices and is verifiably correct by the local-to-global constraints encoded in the adjacency checks and the cycle closure. Implementation notes: Keep cols ≤ 8 so that the state space 2^c remains tractable; the verifier enforces non-triviality by bounds and by requiring S > 100. The generator ensures k ≤ floor(c/2) − 1 and that at least one valid first row exists to avoid degenerate instances.
source_question: The number of ways to color an \(n \times n\) chessboard with black and white such that no neighboring two blocks can be black simultaneously is \(x_n\). Find \(\sum_{n=2}^5 x_n\)．
